hints: For each value in the second array you only need a yes/no answer: does it exist in the first array? Which structure answers that in O(1)?
Put the first array in a hash set. Collect values of the second array that are in it into a second set (so duplicates count once), then sort what you collected.

1. Read both arrays.
  2. Put array 1 into set A.
  3. For each value of array 2 that is in A, add it to set common.
  4. If common is empty, print -1.
  5. Otherwise sort it and print the values separated by spaces.

approaches.name: Brute force
approaches.idea: For each value of the second array, scan the whole first array, and skip values already printed.

approaches.name: Better
approaches.idea: Sort both arrays and walk them with two pointers, skipping duplicates.
approaches.time: O(N log N + M log M)

approaches.name: Optimal
approaches.idea: Hash set of the first array, collect matches into a set, then sort only the matches.
approaches.time: O(N + M + K log K), K = number of common values

explain: For 1 2 2 1 and 2 2, set A = {1, 2}. Both 2s from the second array are in A, but the common set keeps only one 2, so we print 2. In the second sample nothing from 2 4 is in {1, 3, 5}, so the result is empty and we print -1. A TreeSet in Java keeps the matches sorted automatically.
recognize: "Values present in both lists, each once" → set lookup for membership, a set for uniqueness.
python:
import sys
data = list(map(int, sys.stdin.read().split()))
n = data[0]
a = set(data[1:1 + n])
m = data[1 + n]
b = set(data[2 + n:2 + n + m])
common = sorted(a & b)
print(" ".join(map(str, common)) if common else -1)
